summary: Confirmed DONE (60633eff3, #710; also in the Hub's vendored 7bc39eec3). The shared client subscribes with replay:"metadata". The server marks connect-time catch-up `started` events with replay:true, history "" and hasRunningSubprocess. In applyTerminalEvent, a replay takes the registerThreadTerminal path, which never sets terminalOpen or changes the active terminal or group. Force-open now only happens on live started/restarted. Reconciliation drops replays that prove nothing was missed. A mounted drawer that accepts a replay re-hydrates with terminal.open(sinceCursor) instead of wiping its scrollback. Because ChatTerminalShell mounts the drawer only when terminalOpen is true, a closed drawer no longer loads the xterm chunk or issues terminal.open on reload or reconnect. The server only replays at subscribe, Manager.open reattach emits no event, and mobile ignores terminal events, so no other replay path remains. Two side notes, neither a reason to reopen this finding: (1) A live `started` from another device's terminal.open is broadcast to every subscriber and still force-opens the drawer on all other web clients. That is intended semantics for server-initiated starts, so changing it is a separate product decision. (2) On a device with no stored state for the thread, the fix leaves the placeholder `default` terminal focused (see fixDefects).

evidence.note: `started` gains an optional `replay: true` plus `hasRunningSubprocess`, both documented as catch-up-only.
TerminalSubscribeEventsInput { replay?: "metadata" }. The old server payload was Schema.Struct({}), so old servers ignore the field.
terminalBootstrapEvent emits replay:true with history "" for metadata subscribers. Legacy subscribers keep the full snapshot.
Only running sessions are replayed, once per subscription. Live events behind the snapshot cursor are filtered out.
A reattach in Manager.open returns openSnapshot and publishes no `started`, so a reopen is not a second replay path.
The single shared subscription site always passes { replay: "metadata" }.
`replay || quiet` goes through registerThreadTerminal. setThreadActiveTerminal and setThreadTerminalOpen(true) now run only for live starts. Old code at f1be4abc7 called both unconditionally.
registerThreadTerminal adds an unknown id and restores terminalOpen, activeTerminalId and activeTerminalGroupId.
A replay is accepted only when its cursor is past the highest output or activity sequence already accounted for, or the generation is new.
A replay carries running-subprocess state through, and unknown leaves the state unchanged.
A drawer that accepts a replay keeps appliedCursor and calls openTerminal({resync:true}), which asks for sinceCursor=appliedCursor (lines 1001-1018). Repeated replays are rejected, so it cannot loop.
drawerOpen still requires terminalState.terminalOpen, so a closed drawer stays unmounted at boot.
The web sink passes events unchanged into the shared store, with no second force-open path.
Mobile ignores terminal events (applyTerminalEvent is a no-op).
Store tests: replay keeps the drawer closed and the active terminal unchanged, registers an unknown terminal without focusing it, a live start still opens, and a redundant replay is not buffered.
Server tests cover metadata replay without history and legacy full snapshots.
Browser tests: a caught-up replay keeps scrollback, and a missed reconnect re-hydrates from the history after the view's cursor.

fixDefects: One minor edge case, not a correctness bug. On a device with no stored terminal state for the thread (new browser or device, or cleared storage), the store starts from the default state: terminalIds ["default"], active "default". registerThreadTerminal adds a replayed non-default terminal (for example terminal-<uuid>, or one running after the user closed `default` elsewhere) as an unfocused group. When the user later opens the drawer, the placeholder `default` is active, so terminal.open spawns a brand-new shell and the user lands on it instead of the running one. The old code focused the replayed terminal. store.test.ts:90-98 asserts this exact outcome (terminalIds [default, background], active default). The proposal itself asked for no focus change, so this is an accepted trade-off rather than a regression of the finding. It affects only first use on a new device, and its value is low. Separately and out of scope: a live `started` from another client's terminal.open is published to every subscriber (Manager.startSession publishEvent) and still force-opens and refocuses the drawer on all other web clients.
implementationSketch: Optional polish for the fresh-device edge case. In packages/client-runtime/src/state/terminal/store.ts applyTerminalEvent, when a replay registers a terminal for a threadKey with no entry in state.terminalStateByThreadKey (no state stored on this device) and the current active terminal is the untouched default placeholder, make the replayed terminal active without opening. Do this only for the first replay that creates the entry: listSessions sorts by updatedAt descending, so that is the most recently used session, and later replays find the entry present and keep focus. Leave terminalOpen false. Add a store.test.ts case: with no prior state, replaying `background` then `default` keeps terminalOpen=false and makes `background` active only when `default` was not itself replayed first. Keep the existing 'keeps a closed drawer closed' test unchanged. Not needed to close this finding.
decisionReason: Nothing remains for this finding. The optional fresh-device focus tweak and the cross-device live-start behaviour are UX trade-offs. If pursued, the live-start one would need a product call on whether starts from other clients should open the drawer, but it is outside this finding's scope.
correction: No correction to the status. The auditor's line ranges are accurate. Two additions: the fix is also in the Hub's vendored Ryco (60633eff3 is an ancestor of 7bc39eec3), and the fresh-device placeholder-focus trade-off is now noted.
